heuristics: H1 coverage: the 6N^2(1 - 1/L) distinct rationals a w/(u a' w') hit z nearly like independent uniform elements of H: at production size |R|/m >= 1 - e^-K - 0.0005, a coverage within the census deviation (1 - e^-K = 0.390733 rounded down at K = 0.4955; success at least 0.390217 after every failure term and this allowance). z is uniform in H and independent of the lists, so P(z is an off-diagonal candidate) = |R|/m exactly, R the mu6 multiples of the off-diagonal ratios. Support: an exact census of R on toy primes built by the production rules (evidence.py mode census; proof Section 6): at K = 0.4955, 1907 distinct primes at m from 2^30 to 2^35.24 give |R|/m - (1 - e^-K) with per-size means +0.000044 to +0.000113 and lowest prime -0.000232 (136 of 504 at 2^30 lie below 1 - e^-K), -0.000215 from 2^31 up and -0.000099 from 2^32 up; at K = 0.4965, 74 primes over the same sizes have lowest -0.000073; at K = 0.4975, 84 primes have lowest -0.000108; at K = 0.50, 128 primes from 2^30 up have lowest -0.000210, no prime from 2^28 up falls more than 0.0005 below and one of 20 at 2^26 falls 0.00052 below; the success line carries the 0.0005 as an explicit term, and after it 0.000217 remains above the required 0.39; at the lowest K = 0.4955 prime the margin over 0.39 is 0.000485 (2.0 times that prime; the allowance covers it 2.1 times), while 0.000717 is tolerated before 0.39 and 0.000517 before the claim (3.0 and 2.2 times the prime). Toy index 2^2 to 2^10, product sizes and m (up to 2^35.24 against 2^234.857) differ from production, so the census supports H1 and does not prove it; production success rests on H1

H2/H2' H-prime availability over the exact windows the capped searches examine, supported by the density 1/2^20 among primes: the primes in (2^39, 2^78], all within the 2^73 H-tests charged, hold at least L (below 2^51.6296) H-primes (expected above 2^52.24, 1.53 L); the first 2^86 primes above 2^80, all inside the sieved (2^80, 2^80 + 2^92], hold at least 2^65 (expected 2^66); at most 16 walk-list gaps exceed 2^33 and none 2^34 (exponential gaps, expected number above 2^33 below 2^-166.9); on a shortage the run stops with no scalar

H3 key bits: 192-bit parity y-keys behave as independent uniform strings across mu6 orbits (bucket occupancy, comparison and false-match caps; toy chi-square 31.32 vs 31, consistent with the model at toy size; the production independence and concentration every cap uses rest on H3)
limitations: Analytic bound; no full-size run. Instruction counts itemised, not measured on hardware.
Memory is exponential (2^122.8123 bytes, the exact itemised sum over all nodes at full allocation, asserted as an integer inequality; records alone below 2^120.63).

Per-node comparison cap, per-slot cap, candidate caps at owner and generating nodes, re-walk cap and node overflow make the run fail with total probability below 2^-20 + 2^-40 under H3, given at most 2^15 off-diagonal true matches; more than 2^15 has probability below 2^-16.01 by Markov's inequality on their exact mean K(1 - 1/L) over uniform z, with no heuristic; the diagonal true-match event (z = a/(u a') for one base pair gives L > 2^44 candidates, so the run outputs fail) adds at most 6 x 2^128 / m < 2^-104.27; every tail, cost and memory figure is rounded up and every success figure down; charged work is the maximum, not the expectation.

Depends on the walk-with-one-addition idea of cbadde77, the H-prime semiprime construction of 6ecec8e3 / cf6d45a8 and the bucket-matching package of 0a45ddb2; the one parameter change from 0a45ddb2 is K = 0.4955 instead of 0.52, and the queued receive path is replaced by one mailbox per link with no queue and no polling (Section 2); its true-match tail (now with the diagonal event) and its Lemma 4 key-equality sentence are corrected, H2 is stated over the searched windows, and every field inversion is named and charged (the shared F_p inversion of each round: 4 instructions per record inside the 180 charged, plus ledger rows for the gap tables, the re-walks and the F_r inversions forming the six z), the scalar-multiplication, H-test and Lemma 1 prices are counted from the cost model in proof Section 4, the sieve is itemised there (crossings-off, per-segment start offsets, the streaming of its sieving primes from the storage nodes, survivor hand-off) and charged 128 instructions per integer, 1.94 times the largest per-integer count, the split-gap walk overhead and re-walk split steps are charged by name, and a census mode counts the H1 coverage exactly on toy primes.
